interactions.summary: Jiang tests why beauty could lead to love, harvesting student answers about design, symmetry, and truth before asserting that great art gives access to the mind of God and thereby activates virtue.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led exchange with student metaphysical proposals

claims.claim: Jiang accepts symmetry as the key mediating concept between beauty and truth, using it to argue that beautiful form hints at a larger intelligible design.
Jiang distinguishes fact from truth by arguing that truth would require a total account of causes and contexts that finite journalism cannot provide but God can.
Jiang's main thesis here is that the mathematical principles within beauty lead the viewer toward the mind of God, and that contact with this divine truth awakens love and virtue.
A student challenge that this sounds Platonic becomes the transition to the next packet's explicit contrast between Plato and Jiang's pro-art view.

signature_moments.moment: Truth is defined negatively against mere factual fragments because only a total perspective could actually hold all the relevant causes together.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It explains why Jiang needs God, not journalism, as the destination of beauty.

signature_moments.moment: Great artwork becomes a portal into the very mind of God.
signature_moments.source_phrase: gives you access into the very mind of God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the lecture's most sweeping claim about why beauty could make a person virtuous.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Truth is treated as total intelligible reality rather than isolated correct facts.
Symmetry is presented as a visible mathematical principle inside beauty that points beyond surface appearance toward truth.

chronology_notes.note: The lecture moves from art's emotional effects to a full metaphysical account in which beauty, symmetry, truth, God, love, and virtue form one chain.

uncertainty_notes.note: One student contribution about bodily curves is casual and underdeveloped; the packet's durable line of argument comes from symmetry, truth, and design rather than that aside.
